flawed_step: Step 2: Inferring E[X_3 | sigma(X_1,X_2)] = E[E[X_3 | sigma(X_2)] | sigma(X_1,X_2)] = X_2. This reverses the tower property: knowing the conditional expectation given sigma(X_2) does not determine the conditional expectation given the larger natural filtration.
assessment_summary: Step 1 (n=1) is justified because F_1 = sigma(X_1). The proof fails for n=2: the assumption conditions only on X_2, whereas the martingale condition also conditions on X_1. Earlier information can affect the conditional expectation of X_3 even after X_2 is known, so the statement is not valid in general.
